clues: A rare wild goat survives in a landscape where cliffs separate high grasslands from deep valleys.
Long erosion of an elevated plateau has left jagged peaks and exceptionally steep escarpments.
Some of the precipices descend about 1,500 metres, making changes in elevation a defining feature.
This protected mountain landscape lies on the Ethiopian plateau and shelters gelada baboons.
Look in northern Ethiopia for the national park whose highland cliffs shelter the endemic Walia ibex.
targetLabel: Simien Mountains National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The protected landscape links erosion of a high plateau with habitats for rare highland animals. The target is the park’s published reference point, not a particular summit or an animal observation site.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
